findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" but later states "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period"
findings.fix: Clarify whether the log is published quarterly or after enrollment periods, and whether people operations, benefits team, or both are responsible.
findings.violation: The publication frequency (quarterly vs. enrollment period) and responsible party (people operations vs. benefits team) are inconsistent for what appears to be the same log.

findings.evidence: "the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email"
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph or move it to a separate troubleshooting section; replace with a description of the normal review process and timeline.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This paragraph describes a specific operational incident rather than standard policy procedure.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist"
findings.fix: Clarify the manager's authority - either they must follow the checklist or they have discretion to approve items outside it, but not both.
findings.violation: This contradicts the earlier statement in Approval Timeline that "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," leaving unclear whether the manager can override the checklist or must follow it.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time"
findings.violation: This sentence is awkwardly phrased and redundant, since reimbursement by definition offsets already-incurred costs.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition and the policy administrator may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: Uses informal second/first person pronouns ("you/we") inconsistent with the formal third-person tone throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: Section titled "Terminology Notes" but contains procedural descriptions, not terminology definitions.
findings.fix: Rename to "Request Processing Steps" or "Process Timeline" to reflect the actual content.
findings.violation: The title does not accurately describe the section's content, misleading the reader about what to expect.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form...you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there"
findings.fix: Rewrite using third person: "Employees record the stipend item on the request form...Employees submit the request in the portal. They track its status there."
findings.violation: Uses informal second-person pronouns ("you") repeatedly, inconsistent with the formal, third-person tone used elsewhere in the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt"
findings.fix: Provide the complete sequence of steps in order, or move this to a different section and replace with a reference.
findings.violation: Incomplete and vague; the phrase "begins with" implies additional steps follow, but no other steps are listed.

findings.evidence: "Overview" section heading and content duplicate "Program Overview" section appearing earlier, with conflicting publication timing ("after every open enrollment period" vs. "each quarter").
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate "Overview" section or consolidate both sections into a single Program Overview with consistent information.
findings.location: Document structure, Overview section appears after Request Steps
findings.violation: Duplicate section headings cause confusion, and conflicting timing information contradicts the earlier section.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out"
findings.fix: Explain why the $200 threshold was chosen (e.g., "requests exceeding 200 dollars require additional financial review").
findings.violation: The $200 review threshold is stated without explanation or justification, despite the maximum stipend being $500.
